chapters.title: We the Travellers – I
covers: Adds thousands in a row and reads the answer up to ten thousand
Places counting tokens in a place value chart of ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones
Writes a number in figures and in words, such as ten thousand fifty-eight
Talks about how people travelled long ago and how many vehicles are in their state
Asks family elders about a past trip and works out its distance and duration

chapters.title: Fractions
topics: comparing fractions of the same whole
covers: Decides whether one third of a chocolate is bigger than one half of another, and explains that the wholes must be the same
Shades parts of grids and finds fractions that are equal, such as 1/3 and 2/6
Uses a fraction kit to find how many small pieces fit into a larger piece
Makes a whole using only certain pieces from the kit
Divides shapes into more equal parts to show a fraction in more than one way

chapters.title: Angles as Turns
topics: right, acute, obtuse and straight angles
covers: Plays a statue game turning a full turn, a half turn and a quarter turn
Finds turns in everyday things such as a giant wheel and the minute hand
Works out what two half turns in the same direction make
Learns the names right, acute, obtuse and straight for different sized angles

chapters.title: We the Travellers – II
topics: addition and subtraction of large numbers
the link between addition and subtraction
covers: Swaps numbers between two groups to make two sums equal, using the fewest swaps
Subtracts 82 minus 37 by regrouping tens into ones and checks by adding back
Works out fuel left or used for different vehicles, from motorbikes to trains
Uses facts such as 67 minus 21 to find related facts like 67 minus 46
Finds sums of consecutive numbers, such as 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10

chapters.title: Far and Near
covers: Chooses metres or centimetres for the height of India Gate, a handkerchief and a mobile phone
Matches lengths of saris and stoles written in cm with the same lengths written in metres
Compares lengths such as 456 cm and 5 m using the signs for greater than, less than and equal to
Learns that 1,000 metres make one kilometre and works out how many ropes make 1 km
Plans water stations for a kilometre race

chapters.title: The Dairy Farm
covers: Finds the numbers hidden behind shapes in multiplication puzzles
Shows that 3 times 2 and 2 times 3 give the same product, and tests other pairs
Works out how many pouches fit into each arrangement of rows and columns that make 60
Multiplies by 10 and 100 by looking at the pattern of zeros
Uses clues to find a two-digit number that is a multiple of 9 and odd

chapters.title: Shapes and Patterns
covers: Makes a paper mat by cutting slits in folded paper and weaving two colours of strips over and under
Looks at woven baskets and talks about the weaving patterns
Names the shapes in a pattern, including rhombuses and parallelograms
Tries to fit shapes together with no gaps to make a tessellation
Finds right angles in the shapes used to build the pattern

chapters.title: Weight and Capacity
covers: Checks a list of item weights and ticks the ones written in a sensible unit
Reads weighing scales with kilograms and grams, and works out what the pointer shows
Converts 3 kg 500 g into grams and back
Compares fruits such as watermelon and pineapple to find the heaviest and lightest
Works out capacity in litres and millilitres for containers and bottles

chapters.title: Coconut Farm
topics: division as the reverse of multiplication
covers: Writes two division facts from one multiplication fact shown as an array of coconuts
Learns that dividend equals divisor times quotient, and uses it to check answers
Fills in the missing factor in a division such as 150 divided by 3
Divides by 10, 20 and 100, and notices what happens to the quotient
Fills a place value chart for division problems

chapters.title: Symmetrical Designs
covers: Cuts out the letter A by folding paper in half and drawing half the letter along the fold
Folds paper into quarters to cut out the letter H, which has two lines of symmetry
Decides which letters can be cut out by drawing only half of them
Finds the lines of symmetry in letters and shapes
Makes symmetrical designs and checks them by folding

chapters.title: Grandmother's Quilt
covers: Works out the perimeter of a square with equal sides, and chooses the right length of lace to cover a border
Draws two rectangles that each have a given perimeter such as 26 cm or 18 cm
Counts the square patches used to make a rug
Covers a table with triangles, circles, squares and rectangles and talks about which covers it best
Learns the difference between perimeter (around a shape) and area (the space inside)

chapters.title: Racing Seconds
covers: Estimates how many seconds everyday actions take, such as blinking or washing hands, then checks by timing
Works out start time, finish time and time spent practising yoga
Finds how much time has passed between two clock times, such as 1:15 pm and 1:42 pm
Converts times between 12-hour and 24-hour formats
Compares how long three children took to paint a picture and names the longest and shortest

chapters.title: Animal Jumps
covers: Finds the missing multiplier when numbers come out of a box
Makes arrays for numbers such as 12 and lists its factors
Lists the multiples of two numbers, such as 4 and 6, and finds the common ones
Checks whether a number is a common factor of two numbers, such as 24 and 36
Works out which numbers an animal lands on when it jumps 5 or 10 steps from zero

chapters.title: Maps and Locations
covers: Works out north, south, east and west when facing the rising sun
Says which way a person's left and right hands point when facing a direction
Follows a bus route on a map from a stop, naming the direction at each step
Describes where a house, park or market is from a landmark
Makes a direction arrow for their own room

chapters.title: Data Through Pictures
topics: true or false questions about data
covers: Collects classmates' TV viewing hours and records them in a table
Answers questions such as how many children watch TV for less than two hours
Reads a pictograph where one icon stands for several items, such as 5 toys
Counts the two-wheelers passing a point on three days using icons
Records daily routines in a table and reads what they show
